solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swayed right away in discussion that went to one's head?

indicators.note: in means the shortened swaying word sits inside the word for discussion

parts.note: a chat is a discussion

indicators.note: away tells us the letter for right is dropped from the swaying word

parts.note: rocked means swayed

explanation.surface: A heated debate that rocked someone and went to their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' and 'in' are the two signals. The question mark flags that the definition is literal: a hat is something that goes onto one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocked hat is headgear with the brim turned up, so it is something worn on the head.

clue.text: Firm female garment, one with hood

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is an item of women's underwear

explanation.surface: A company's women's garment comes with a hood attached.
explanation.definitionFit: The cobra is a venomous snake that spreads a hood of skin around its neck when threatened.

clue.text: Ruler's first-rate son leaves suitably dressed and accompanied

parts.note: Caesar was a Roman ruler; with the 's it gives CAESARS
A means first-rate, as in an A grade
a lad is a boy or son

explanation.surface: The ruler's excellent son goes off appropriately clothed and with company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' reads as the son departing, but it is the noun: salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caesar salad is lettuce leaves tossed in a creamy dressing and served with croutons and parmesan.

clue.text: Anarchic Senorita disregarding king and country

indicators.note: anarchic means chaotic, so the letters are thrown into disorder
disregarding tells us the letter for king is left out of the jumbled letters

parts.note: R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A rebellious Spanish young woman ignores the monarch and the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic nation in northern Europe, bordering Latvia and Russia.

clue.text: Ambassador's worried about technology delay

indicators.note: about means the two words go around the abbreviation for technology

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador; with the 's it gives HES
ate means worried, as in 'what's eating you'
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A diplomat is anxious about computer systems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' works on the whole phrase: 'Ambassador's worried' is read as 'he has worried', with technology placed in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause before acting, which is to delay.

clue.text: Shoddy attempt to grab what remains

indicators.note: to grab means the word for attempt seizes the remains inside itself

parts.note: a try is an attempt
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A poor effort to snatch the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy describes something cheap and of poor quality, which is shoddy.

clue.text: Very penetrating remedy for wind

indicators.note: penetrating means the letter for very goes into the word for remedy

parts.note: a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A powerful treatment for flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as the noun (flatulence) but is the verb, rhyming with 'find'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to bend or twist, which is to curve, as a road winds or curves.

clue.text: Traffic controller about to enter continental city

indicators.note: about means the word for traffic controller goes around the word for entering

parts.note: a traffic cone guides traffic round roadworks
to log is to enter a record, as in a logbook

explanation.surface: A traffic officer is about to go into a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to enter' reads as one phrase meaning almost entering; it splits into 'about' (around) and 'to enter' (LOG).
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a large city in western Germany, on the European continent.

clue.text: Argument with servicemen raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A dispute with soldiers that has been brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with 'cow', is a noisy quarrel or argument.

clue.text: Provokes three cardinals admitting sex

indicators.note: admitting means the three compass letters let the word for sex in among them

parts.note: the cardinal points of the compass include E, N and S
gender is a person's sex

explanation.surface: Three senior churchmen cause a stir by confessing to sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' suggests church princes; here they are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender something is to cause or give rise to it, which is to provoke it.

clue.text: Whinge from Liberal in defeat

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for Liberal inside the word for defeat

parts.note: to beat is to defeat
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in UK politics

explanation.surface: A sore loser's moan from the Liberal party after losing an election.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleat is to complain in a feeble, whining way, which is to whinge.

clue.text: Rogue caught accomplice dividing spoils

indicators.note: dividing means these letters split the word for spoils into two parts

parts.note: swag is loot or spoils
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ally is a helper or accomplice

explanation.surface: A villain is arrested while his partner in crime shares out the loot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a mischievous person or rascal, a mild word for a rogue.

clue.text: Haitian gangster moving unnaturally?

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the two words are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal from Haiti who walks in an odd, unnatural way.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against the grain means acting contrary to one's nature or inclination, so unnaturally; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: A harsh, restricted lifestyle in productive industry

indicators.note: restricted means cut short, so the word for harsh loses its last letter

parts.note: grim means harsh or stern
a culture is a way of life, a lifestyle

explanation.surface: A tough, constrained way of living within a busy manufacturing sector.
explanation.definitionFit: Agriculture is farming, the industry that produces crops and livestock.

clue.text: Irregular therapy disheartened sufferer

parts.note: casual work is irregular, not regular

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart is taken out, leaving only the first and last letters of therapy

explanation.surface: An occasional course of treatment left the patient feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: A casualty is someone injured or harmed, a victim or sufferer of an accident or attack.

clue.text: Arrived on pitch behind gunners, wary of being shot

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, means the first word sits on top of what follows
behind means the word for pitch comes after the gunners

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
to shy is to pitch or throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: Someone reached the field behind the artillery, nervous of being fired on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests gunfire to suit the gunners, but means photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: Camera-shy people dislike being photographed, and a photo is a shot.

clue.text: Intimate debilitating disease that's quite shocking

parts.note: a dear friend is a close or intimate one
ME is myalgic encephalomyelitis, chronic fatigue syndrome

explanation.surface: A close friend has a crippling illness, which is very upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear me is an exclamation of surprise or dismay, said at something quite shocking.

clue.text: Autocrat's bizarre act stops journalist dropping leader

indicators.note: stops means the jumbled letters plug the gap in the shortened journalist
dropping leader means the first letter of the word for journalist falls away

parts.note: an editor is a senior journalist

indicators.note: bizarre means strange, so the letters of act are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tyrant's strange behaviour silences a reporter who has lost his boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping leader', 'bizarre' and 'stops' are the three signals; the scrambled CTA goes after the first two letters of the shortened journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictator is a ruler with absolute power, an autocrat.

clue.text: Woman, following bloke, contracted illness

indicators.note: following means the word for woman comes after the shortened bloke
contracted means shortened, so the word for bloke loses its last letter

parts.note: a bloke is a man
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A woman caught a disease from a man she was seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like catching a disease in the surface, but it shortens MAN to MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is a disease or ailment, a formal word for an illness.

clue.text: Arduous time following drunkard's last dry spell

indicators.note: following means the rough time comes after the drunkard's final letter
last picks the final letter of the word drunkard

parts.note: rough means hard or arduous, as in a rough day

explanation.surface: A tough period after a heavy drinker's final drink, a stretch on the wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry spell' suggests a drinker going sober; it is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long period without rain, a dry spell of weather.

clue.text: Bird nesting in the said overturned bush

indicators.note: nesting in means the bird sits inside the reversed word, like a bird in a nest
overturned means the word for the said is turned the other way round

parts.note: such can mean the aforementioned or the said, as in 'no such person'
the ibis is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: A bird has made its nest in a shrub that has been tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' gives HCUS, and 'nesting in' sets the bird after its first letter. 'the said' is an old-fashioned legal sense of such.
explanation.definitionFit: The hibiscus is a flowering shrub of warm climates, so a kind of bush.

clue.text: Press agent primarily recalled for one period of change

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of agent
recalled means called back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: EG, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: A press agent was first called back for a single period.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age was the era when iron tools replaced bronze, a time of great technological change.

clue.text: Cooker installed in N America gets extended service period

indicators.note: installed in means the cooker is fitted inside the abbreviation

parts.note: NA is the abbreviation for North America
an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: A stove fitted in North America comes with a long guarantee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests a warranty; it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A novena is a Catholic devotion of prayers said over nine successive days.

clue.text: Mistakenly order action doll operated remotely

indicators.note: mistakenly says these letters are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone accidentally orders a doll from a toy range by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio-controlled models are steered by radio signals from a distance, so worked remotely.

clue.text: Border south of duke's abode

indicators.note: south of, in a down clue, means the border word sits below the duke's letter

parts.note: a welt is a strengthened border or edge, as on a shoe or garment

explanation.surface: A boundary below the duke's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abode' looks like a noun for home; it is the past tense of abide, meaning lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Abode, past tense of abide, means resided or lived, as does dwelt.

clue.text: Most fuzzy bats disgust me

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that bats revolt them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals as the subject of the sentence, but it is the adjective meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Smudgiest is the superlative of smudgy, blurred or smeared, so the most fuzzy.

clue.text: Woman in Verdun assaulted

indicators.note: in means the name is concealed within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A woman was attacked in the French town of Verdun.
explanation.definitionFit: Una is a female given name, so in crosswords a woman.

clue.text: Before service, sailor curses?

indicators.note: before says the sailor goes ahead of the word for service

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
use is service, as in getting good use out of something

explanation.surface: A sailor swears before going on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuse is insulting language, and curses are swear words, so the plural noun fits as a collective idea.

clue.text: Brewing ingredient? It's put back in still

indicators.note: in puts the turned-round letters inside the word for still

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'yet more'

indicators.note: put back means the letters are reversed

parts.note: it is a slang word for sex appeal, SA; the 's is it is, joining to the rest

explanation.surface: A brewer asks whether an ingredient is returned to the distilling apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' suggests the distilling vessel; it is the adverb. 'put back' makes AS, and 'in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast ferments sugars into alcohol, so it is a key ingredient in brewing beer.

clue.text: Alpha males engaged in welcome correspondence

parts.note: alpha is A in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: engaged in means the males are held inside the word for welcome

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
men are males

explanation.surface: Dominant men take part in a friendly exchange of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' suggests letters, but here means a match or agreement between things.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence can mean conformity or match between things, which is agreement.
